package_info.why_malicious: These packages are dependency confusion attacks, published to npm with names mimicking John Deere's internal/private packages. Their purpose is to trick build systems into installing attacker-controlled code, potentially allowing code execution or data exfiltration in targeted environments.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or postinstall (depending on package.json scripts)
execution_context.file_location: index.js or main entrypoint (could also be in package.json scripts)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Prints a message to the console or exfiltrates environment variables to an external server, demonstrating code execution if the package is installed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes automatically upon import or install, and may exfiltrate sensitive data or demonstrate unauthorized code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not execute arbitrary code or exfiltrate environment variables on install/import. Legitimate packages do not contact external servers without user action.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate postinstall scripts may perform setup or telemetry (with user consent), but not exfiltrate sensitive data.
key_indicators: Console messages indicating a test or PoC

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a package to npm with a name matching a John Deere internal dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Target build system installs the malicious package instead of the intended internal one.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in the package executes upon install or import, potentially exfiltrating environment variables or demonstrating code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives proof of code execution or sensitive data from the target environment.

behavioral_signatures: Packages with names mimicking internal/private dependencies
Automatic execution of code on install/import
Network requests to external domains during install/import
Console output indicating dependency confusion testing
file_indicators: Presence of suspicious postinstall scripts in package.json
index.js/main file with exfiltration or test code
References to external domains in code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to unknown or attacker-controlled domains (e.g., webhook.site, attacker.com)
Unexpected network activity during package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages with names similar to internal dependencies being published to public registries. Flag packages that execute code on install/import, especially those making outbound network requests or printing unexpected messages. Use network monitoring to detect exfiltration attempts during build or install processes. Review package.json scripts and entrypoint files for suspicious behavior.
